record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Prove exponential screening in the two-dimensional Coulomb gas at temperatures that are not especially small, possibly all the way down to the Kosterlitz-Thouless transition.

evidence.quote: Prove exponential screening in the 2D Coulomb gas at not particularly small temperatures (down to the KT transition?).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional lattice Coulomb gas on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ defined as follows. To each site $x \in \Lambda \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ assign an integer charge $q_x \in \mathbb{Z}$, and consider the grand-canonical partition function
$$ Z_\Lambda(\beta, z) = \sum_{\{q_x\}_{x\in\Lambda}} \Bigl( \prod_{x\in\Lambda} z^{|q_x|} \mathbf{1}_{q_x\ne 0} + \mathbf{1}_{q_x=0} \Bigr)\, \mathbf{1}\!\left\{ \sum_{x\in\Lambda} q_x = 0 \right\}\, \exp\!\Bigl( -\beta \sum_{x\ne y} q_x q_y\, G(x,y) \Bigr), $$
where $G(x,y)$ is the two-dimensional lattice Coulomb potential (which behaves like $-\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\log|x-y|$ at large separation), $\beta>0$ is the inverse temperature, and $z>0$ is the fugacity. Let $\langle\,\cdot\,\rangle_{\beta,z}$ denote the corresponding infinite-volume Gibbs expectation (any subsequential limit as $\Lambda\uparrow\mathbb{Z}^2$).

The truncated two-point charge correlation
$$ S(x,y) \;=\; \langle q_x\, q_y \rangle_{\beta,z} - \langle q_x \rangle_{\beta,z}\langle q_y\rangle_{\beta,z} $$
is said to exhibit exponential screening if there exist constants $C, m>0$ such that $|S(x,y)| \le C \exp(-m|x-y|)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^2$.

It is known (Brydges–Federbush; Yang) that exponential screening holds at sufficiently high temperature (small $\beta$) and small fugacity, and it is known (Fröhlich–Spencer) that at sufficiently low temperature (large $\beta$) and small fugacity the system is in a non-screening Kosterlitz–Thouless phase with power-law decay.

Problem. Prove that exponential screening of the truncated charge–charge correlation $S(x,y)$ holds throughout the entire high-temperature (plasma) phase of the two-dimensional Coulomb gas — in particular, at inverse temperatures $\beta$ that are not assumed to be especially small, and ideally for all $\beta$ strictly below the Kosterlitz–Thouless critical inverse temperature $\beta_{\mathrm{KT}}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Exponential (Debye) screening for the 2D Coulomb gas is rigorously known only in a perturbative regime: at high temperature with small activity (Brydges; Brydges–Federbush; Yang). On the other side, Fröhlich–Spencer rigorously established the existence of the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition and a non-screening phase at low temperatures. Extending the proof of exponential screening up to the KT transition (or even to moderate temperatures beyond the small-β/small-z regime) does not appear to have been achieved in the literature; the question is still discussed as an open problem in constructive field theory.

status_evidence.title: The Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in two-dimensional abelian spin systems and the Coulomb gas (Fröhlich–Spencer)
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous proof of KT transition in 2D Coulomb gas via inductive multiscale expansion in the sine-Gordon representation for sufficiently large β and small activity.
status_evidence.claim: Low-temperature non-screening phase is rigorously established only for large β and small activity, leaving the intermediate regime open.

status_evidence.title: Critical exponents of the 2D Coulomb gas at the BKT transition
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes power-law decay with logarithmic corrections along the transition curve at small activity.
status_evidence.claim: At the KT transition (small activity), correlations decay as power laws, not exponentially; pinpointing the screening regime up to KT remains a subtle open question.
